الإثم = sin, being burdened with guilt (آثم، أثيم، مأثوم). λυόμεθα = we are being released/loosened. This is a genuine conceptual pair: the concept of being freed from sin (λύω τὰς ἁμαρτίας) is central to both Semitic and Greek religious thought. Release from guilt is the natural complement of guilt itself.

Arabic الأسكتان: labia (skin folds at sides of vulva). Greek σκύτινος: made of leather/skin. Both share the semantic field of 'skin/hide material'. The Arabic relates to skin-like anatomical folds; σκύτος = skin. Plausible semantic drift.

الأشقر includes 'من الدم ما صار علقاً' (blood that became clotted). γλίσχρος=sticky, viscous, adhesive. Clotted blood IS sticky/viscous. This is a direct material-property match: coagulated blood shares the exact physical quality described by γλίσχρος.

الآمِص = طعام يتّخذ من لحم عجل بجلده (a food prepared from calf meat with its skin). λαιμός = throat, gullet. Food and the throat are directly linked through the act of eating — food is what passes through the throat. The anatomical pathway of consumption connects them strongly.

الأنس: الإنسي=الأيسر (the left/easier side), ما أقبل عليك (what faces you). Also root أنس=familiarity, ease, comfort. γαληνός=calm, serene (especially of the sea). Both orbit the concept of tranquility, ease, and gentleness. The emotional quality of peaceful comfort connects them.
البثع (blood appearing on lips/skin) ↔ phlebotomia (bloodletting): both concern blood at skin surface

البثنة=الرملة الليّنة (soft sandy ground). πολυβενθής=deep-bottomed, of great depth. Soft sand suggests deep terrain (you sink into it), and πολυβενθής describes deep ground/seabed. Both describe ground with depth quality. The terrain-depth concept is shared.

Arabic البرنس: a tall hood/hood-garment. Greek Βορινός: ancient city between Beirut and Sidon. The Arabic garment name may derive from 'Phoenician-style' covering (برنساء = the people). Plausible that the city name and the garment share a Phoenician origin.
If the Greek term belongs to the λώβη field of harm and ruin, Arabic الداهية shares a strong negative disaster core, giving a plausible semantic chain.

التناوه=ترك المذاكرة (abandoning discussion/study). καταλύω=to dissolve, destroy, bring to an end. Abandoning discussion IS a dissolution/ending of the activity. The cessation concept maps well: ترك (leaving off) parallels κατα-λύω (un-doing).

Arabic الثرم: breaking of a tooth at its root. Greek Θέρμη: Therma (hot springs city, Macedonia). Heat-fever-breaking: the Arabic ثرم includes bodily breaking, the Greek city name means 'hot.' Weak phonological match th-r-m.
The Arabic gloss is an extra teat above the udder; Greek τελέθω expresses coming forth or growing, giving a plausible growth-based chain.

الثين = مستخرج الدرّة من البحر (the pearl diver, one who extracts pearls from the sea). λανθάνομαι = I am hidden, I am concealed (mediopassive of λανθάνω). The pearl is the hidden treasure concealed in the sea depths. The pearl diver's entire profession is to find what λανθάνει (lies hidden). The hidden-thing-in-the-deep connects both concepts directly.
Arabic الجفر: young sheep (fattened), also an unlined well. Greek Γάφαρα: place name. Both share j/g-f-r consonant skeleton; the place may derive from a pastoral/water source term.
To make clear/reveal and the Greek sense of brightness/gleam can meet through a shared notion of manifest visibility.

Arabic الجنث: origin/root (الجنث = الأصل). Greek γενηθείς: aorist passive participle of γίγνομαι (having been born/generated). Origin/root and 'having been generated/born' share the conceptual core of genesis/origin. Strong mafahim match.

Arabic الحذن: waistband, also small-eared animal; الحذنة = buttocks area. Greek χόδανος: buttocks. The Arabic الحذنتان = the two buttocks/labia explicitly matches the Greek 'butt' meaning. Clear semantic match.

Arabic الحرسم: poison, death (also a corner). Greek Χοράσμιοι: Chorasmians (ancient tribe of Chorasmia). The Chorasmians were famous warriors; 'poison/death' as a tribal characterization. Consonant match h-r-s-m / kh-r-s-m. Plausible ethnonym derivation.
مقاربة الخطا والكلام carries a core of closeness and sticking-together that plausibly matches sticky or adhesive.

الخضا: تفتّت الشيء الرطب / وانفضاخه (crumbling/breaking apart of moist matter). οὐλοχύται=barley grains poured over sacrificial victim. Both involve granular matter being broken/scattered. Crumbling moist substance and scattered grain share the particulate-dispersion concept.

Arabic الخفر: (1) intense modesty/shyness; (2) to give protection, escort, guard. Greek ἐχέφρων = holding one's mind, thoughtful, prudent (ἔχω=hold + φρήν=mind). Both carry a core of restraint combined with protective vigilance; the guard/protector role (خفر) and the prudent mind-holder map closely at the mafahim level.

Arabic is a hand-moved vessel; Greek is to seize or grasp. The shared core is manual handling and taking hold.

السكركة = شراب الذرة (a drink made from sorghum/millet — a thick fermented grain beverage). γλίσχρος = sticky, viscous, adhesive, claggy. A fermented grain drink is characteristically thick and sticky in texture. The Arabic names the substance, the Greek names its primary physical quality. This is a genuine material-property match.

السمع = hearing; اسمع مني = hear from me (imperative). λίσσομαι = I beseech/supplicate. The supplicant begs to be heard; hearing is the goal of supplication. These two words sit at opposite ends of the same communicative act -- the speaker pleads (λίσσομαι) and the listener hears (سمع). Strong functional semantic pair.

الشرنتي = a bird (طائر). λαλίστερος = more talkative/chattering (comparative of λάλος). Birds are the archetypal chatterers in every language. A bird named الشرنتي and an adjective meaning 'more chattering' meet perfectly at the bird-song/chatter intersection.

شعفة=love that overwhelms/covers the heart from above (غشّى الحبّ القلب). διαλυσίφιλος=dissolving friendship/love. Both are about love's transformative power - one overwhelming, the other dissolving. The love domain is shared but the direction differs.
Arabic describes an old lax woman; Greek appears to carry a loosened or dissolved quality, so the core of slackness is plausibly shared.

Arabic الشقف = pottery; broken earthenware shards (كسر الفخار). Greek σκάφη = boat-shaped vessel, tub, basin (earthenware). Both refer directly to pottery/ceramic vessel material; Arabic شقف is earthenware/ceramic and Greek σκάφη is a clay/earthenware vessel. Direct material overlap in the ceramic/pottery domain.

الشمطالة = البضعة من اللحم فيها شحم (a piece of meat with fat). ἵλασμα = propitiation, atonement sacrifice, sin offering. In ancient Semitic and Mediterranean religion, the fat piece of meat IS the offering of atonement. The fatty meat portion was specifically the part offered to the deity. This is a direct ritual-to-substance connection.
